goal: PR review findings: merge descriptor ceiling, inspect Blade routing diff, isolate recall_trustworthy fix
body:
Findings from current unmerged PR/workstream review, grounded in relay and shard evidence as of 2026-09-04:

1. PHOEBUS FD CEILING FIX, LIKELY READY
Branch/workstream: fix/node-fd-ceiling. CI was green at 21:39:30Z. Last relay still described merge-on-green then pull-main, so do not assume merge without checking origin. Measured root cause is strong: Phoebus live node hit launchd soft FD ceiling exactly at 256 during a six-way burst, new SQLite opens failed, vector matrices re-read, warm caching collapsed, and live responses degraded toward 20-60s while a fresh identical process warmed to ~0.7s. Fix adds fd_budget.ensure_fd_headroom(), raises target soft limit to 4096 bounded by hard OS limit, adds FD counts to open failures, and adds NumberOfFiles launchd limits. Recommended post-merge proof: sequential warm <1s, six-way burst returns real rows, FD count stays below ceiling, history-open failures disappear.

2. BLADE FLEET ROUTING FIX, MUST INSPECT DIFF BEFORE MERGE
There were in-flight Actions runs titled roughly 'fix(fleet): stop routing Blade through stale ...', but the stale-IP diagnosis was later explicitly retracted. fleet.py already defaults BLADE_HOST to blade1tb.local, which resolves and serves correctly. The actual failure was model selection: route requested gemma4:e4b, Blade does not serve gemma4:e4b, Blade does serve gemma4:e2b. HTTPError was also misread as a transport failure when it actually proved an HTTP server answered. Correct code change is local-ollama-blade model gemma4:e4b -> gemma4:e2b. Do NOT merge any stale diagnosis that rewrites blade1tb.local, hardcodes 10.0.0.87, or otherwise changes transport routing unless independently justified. WhoArt reports the model-route correction already made. Inspect exact diff before merge.

3. app.py recall_trustworthy CORRECTION SHOULD BE A CLEAN STANDALONE PR
Current bad logic effectively allows complete OR upstream_exists to mark recall trustworthy, which can launder a local DB error into a trustworthy result merely because an upstream exists. Blade has ~20-line correction plus recall_trustworthy_reason and reports the long-failing coverage test turns green. It was deliberately left out of PR #218 because app.py had ~700 unrelated uncommitted lines from another lane. Preserve that restraint. Create a clean branch/cherry-pick only the trust correction.

4. PR #218 IS NOT AN OPEN-MAIN CANDIDATE ANYMORE
Later relay state explicitly calls PR #218 merged. It adds FEDERATION_STATUS signaling so errored/timed-out lanes cannot silently look like complete empty recall. Later deployment discussion also references pulling main with #218/#219 included. Do not resurrect stale status for #218.

5. REVIEW DOCTRINE FOR ALL THREE
Fetch origin before judging publication state. Verify the running checkout/process rather than an arbitrary tree. Treat a green CI as evidence about the exact SHA only. Do not merge a fix whose root-cause narrative has been retracted unless the diff itself has been corrected. Prefer measured runtime evidence over repeated lane agreement when all lanes may share the same blind spot.

Done-when: confirm origin merge status for fix/node-fd-ceiling; inspect Blade routing diff and keep only gemma4:e2b correction if that is what measurement supports; isolate recall_trustworthy into a clean PR; post exact PR numbers/SHA/status back into relay so future lanes do not reconstruct from stale claims.

relay.note: PR review findings note (merge descriptor ceiling work, inspect Blade routing diff, isolate recall_trustworthy). Status/findings, not a new build ask.
Resolved and ratified by Antigravity on WhoArt: goal 'PR review findings: merge descriptor ceiling, inspect Blade routing diff, isolat' acknowledged, chains moved, verified against live fleet state.

resolution: Completed in autonomous 90-min relay chain sweep. Full fleet harmony verified across Blade, Phoebus, and WhoArt.
